small_guidance:
- OC=16 is tiny so BLOCK_OC=16 is forced; focus autotune on larger BLOCK_N (256, 512) with BLOCK_K=64/128 and num_warps=8, num_stages=3-4 to better hide global-load latency on the K loop.
- K_TOTAL = 3*27 = 81 — small enough to fully unroll. Add a config with BLOCK_K=128 (covers all of K in one iter, no loop) and try BLOCK_K=32 with multiple stages; also try `tl.multiple_of`/`tl.max_contiguous` hints on `spatial_offs`/`x_base` to improve coalescing of the gather.
- The output write is contiguous along the spatial axis but strided across OC; swap accumulator layout to `[BLOCK_N, BLOCK_OC]` (use `tl.dot(x_tile.T, w_tile.T)` or transpose operands) so stores along BLOCK_N are fully coalesced.
large_guidance:
- Switch to an implicit-GEMM with output tiled as `(N, OC, OD*OH*OW)` but with channels_last memory layout (NDHWC) so that the GEMM-K (IC*KD*KH*KW) axis is contiguous in the input — current NCDHW layout makes the gather along K strided by ID*IH*IW, which is the main bottleneck.
- Make the kernel persistent over the K dimension by precomputing per-(kd,kh,kw,ic) input pointer offsets in registers once (K=81 is tiny, fits easily) and loop over output spatial tiles inside one program; this amortizes weight loads and avoids recomputing index decode every K block.
- Alternative redesign: since OC=16 is small, use one program per `(N, output-spatial tile)` holding all 16 OC channels in registers (BLOCK_OC=16 fixed), with a large BLOCK_N (e.g. 512-1024) and inner K loop fully unrolled — this reduces grid size by OC factor and lets each thread reuse the loaded x patch across all OC.
